date.description:
The DEVICE'S LOCAL calendar day, `YYYY-MM-DD`.

Not a timestamp, deliberately. A timestamp would have to be bucketed into a
day server-side, and the only day the server can derive is the UTC one —
which puts most Indian morning nitnem (Amrit Vela is 21:30–00:30 UTC the
day before) under the wrong date. The device already knows which day it
was; it just has to say so.

readingSeconds.description: Total seconds READ on this device on this day. Cumulative, not a delta.

listeningSeconds.description: Total seconds LISTENED on this device on this day.

deviceId.description:
Which device these rows belong to. Part of the key, not merely metadata:
a device owns its own row for a date, so two devices on the same day are
summed rather than one overwriting the other.

days.description:
The days this device has changed since it last synced — normally one.

Capped so a corrupt or hostile client cannot make one request rewrite an
account's entire history; 400 days covers a year of backfill with room to
spare.

version.description: App/schema version that produced this snapshot

capturedAt.description:
When the snapshot was captured client-side (ISO-8601). Its calendar day is
the idempotency key — same-day re-syncs upsert (last-write-wins).

deviceId.description:
Which device produced this snapshot. No longer the sync identity — the row
is keyed on the account from the bearer token. Still required, because it
is how snapshots pushed before the user had an account are adopted on their
first authenticated sync.

userId.description:
IGNORED. The owning account is resolved from the bearer token and never
from the body — a request must not be able to nominate whose data it
writes.

Kept only because the shipped app still sends `userId: null` and `main.ts`
sets `forbidNonWhitelisted: true`, so removing it would 400 every existing
client. Delete once the app has stopped sending it.

out into indexed columns.

Client-generated path id (uuid). Supply this so the app can create the

the server mint one.

Days the path was read (ISO "YYYY-MM-DD"). Merged by union with the
server's set — reading days are monotonic and are never removed, so a
device that is behind cannot wipe days recorded elsewhere.

baseUpdatedAt.description:
The `updatedAt` the client last saw for this path (ms since epoch). When
provided, the update is rejected with 409 if the server row is newer —
optimistic concurrency for multi-device edits.

settings.description:
The user's Sehaj Path preferences, returned verbatim as they were saved.
Keys are app-owned (see UpsertSehajPathSettingsDto); the server does not
interpret them.

The user's Sehaj Path preferences, stored verbatim. Keys are owned by the
app so new toggles can ship without a backend change — the server never
interprets these values, it only persists and echoes them. The known keys
today are `fontSize`, `larivaar`, `paragraphMode`, `vishraam`,
`vishraamsSource`, `angsFormat` and `consent`, but any JSON object is
accepted. Overall request size is bounded by the global body-parser limit.

readDates.description: Days the path was read (ISO "YYYY-MM-DD"); merged by union across devices.

startDate.description: When the path was started (ms since epoch)

completionDate.description: When the path was completed (ms since epoch), or null/absent if not.

updatedAt.description:
The device's last-modified clock for this path (ms since epoch). Required —
the merge compares it against the server's copy to decide the winner.

deletedAt.description:
Set when the device deleted this path offline (ms since epoch). Propagates
the deletion to the server and other devices.

pathId.description: Stable path id (uuid) — the match key between this device and the server.

paths.description: The device's full set of local paths (including ones it deleted offline).

lastSyncedAt.description:
When this device last synced (ms since epoch); 0/absent on first sync.
Server tombstones newer than this are returned in `deletedPathIds`.

settings.description:
The device's current settings snapshot (opaque). When present it is applied
and stamped with the SERVER clock — last write to the server wins (no
device clocks involved). Include it only when settings changed locally
since the last sync; omit it otherwise so a stale device cannot overwrite
newer settings from another device.

paths.description:
The authoritative set of the user's live (non-deleted) paths after the
merge. The client should replace its local set with these.

settings.description:
The authoritative settings document after the last-write-wins merge, or
null if the user has none.

syncedAt.description:
Server time of this sync (ms since epoch). Store it verbatim and send it
as `lastSyncedAt` on the next sync — never use the device clock, which may
be skewed against the server's tombstone/merge timestamps.

deletedPathIds.description:
Ids of paths that are deleted server-side (tombstoned by this or another
device). The client should remove these locally.
